$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Every API fact here is read from Google's YouTube v3 discovery document (https://youtube.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v3).
title: YouTube

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Reusable. A refresh response carries access_token, expires_in, scope and token_type — no refresh_token — and Google’s own expiry rule is "the refresh token has not been used for six months", which is a statement about a token that is PERSISTED AND REPLAYED. Under rotation it would change hourly and that rule could never fire.
oauth.$grantComment: ONE consent grant shared by every Google connector (MOIC #1, 2026-11-08). A host may run them all on one OAuth client: request each feature's scopes when it is first used, with include_granted_scopes=true, and Google's new token covers every scope granted before. A refresh token comes back only on the FIRST code exchange with access_type=offline, so keep the stored one when an exchange returns none. Revoking ANY token removes the person's WHOLE grant -- every Google connector, not this one -- so a per-feature disconnect stops using the scope locally and only a full Google disconnect revokes. Identify the account by the id_token's sub (request openid; verify iss and aud = clientId), never by email.
oauth.$restrictedScopesComment: Google's RESTRICTED tier puts the whole OAuth client under verification and an annual CASA assessment. None of this connector's scopes is restricted.
oauth.$scopeComment: playlistItems.insert accepts youtube, youtube.force-ssl and youtubepartner. youtube.force-ssl is narrower than full `Manage your YouTube account` access while still allowing edits to videos and related channel resources, so it is the least authority this action needs; youtubepartner is for content partners.
oauth.$comment: The host performs the browser consent flow and refreshes Google's one-hour access token; refreshToken is required so the connection does not expire after that hour.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED. YouTube exposes no separate test estate. Adding a test video creates a real playlist item on a real YouTube channel.
sandboxNote: YouTube has no sandbox. Every live-mode add changes a real playlist; use the faker during development and remove live test items afterward.
summary: Add videos to YouTube playlists from a workflow or a Laravel app.
$setupComment: Steps read from Google's docs on 2026-11-14 (each cites its page). Every Google connector shares one grant, so the first four steps are the same for all of them; do them once.

setup.title: Create (or reuse) the Google Cloud project for {{appName}}
setup.detail: Every Google connector shares ONE consent grant (oauth.grant "google"), so use one project and one OAuth client for all of them: one consent and one refresh token per person.

setup.title: Enable the YouTube Data API v3
setup.detail: Console: APIs & Services, Library; open the YouTube Data API v3 and click Enable.

setup.title: Configure the consent screen
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Branding (app name {{appName}}, support email, contact email), then Audience: Internal for people inside your Google Workspace organisation only, or External (while it is in testing, add each tester under Test users). Then Data Access, Add or Remove Scopes, and add `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl` beside the scopes of any other Google connector you use. You cannot remove the consent screen once it is configured.

setup.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Clients, Create Client; type Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs click Add URI and paste {{oauthRedirectUrl}}, then Create. Copy the client ID and client secret when the client is created.

setup.title: Connect an account and check it works
setup.detail: Connect one Google account through {{appName}}'s OAuth flow, then run the check below.
setup.prompt: Using {{appName}}'s {{connector}} connection, add a video the person names to a playlist they own with playlist_item_insert, and report the returned item id. Tell them they can remove it.
setup.done: playlist_item_insert returns an id and the video appears in that playlist.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client ID
credentialFields.help: From Google Cloud Console. One value for the whole installation.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client secret
credentialFields.help: The client secret for the same OAuth app.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Per connected YouTube account; expires after one hour.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Per connected YouTube account; the host uses it to refresh the access token.
